findings.title: The new Electron validation test bypasses the required Setup journey
findings.body: This test launches with `skipSetup: true` and goes directly to Settings, so it does not exercise the Setup provider-validation path required by the new spec. It also never checks that continuation/save is disabled after a failed validation. A Setup regression could therefore leave an invalid provider enabled while this added test still passes. Add Setup coverage for 429 and non-auth 400, including assertions that verification is not claimed and continuation is disabled.

findings.title: The cleanup regression assumes an optional environment variable exists
findings.body: Although the surrounding fixture treats `CLAWX_E2E_RUN_ROOT` as optional and falls back to `tmpdir()`, `join(process.env.CLAWX_E2E_RUN_ROOT!, ...)` throws at runtime when the variable is absent. A direct Playwright invocation without that environment variable therefore fails before launching the second app. Use a unique `mkdtemp` directory under `tmpdir()` or derive the profile from an existing unique fixture directory; the current fixed path can also collide across concurrent workers or projects.

overall_explanation: Capturing the real Electron main PID and using it for Windows tree teardown is a sound improvement. However, the final-matrix implementation does not cover the explicitly required Setup validation and disabled-continuation behavior, and its process-cleanup regression can fail when the optional run-root environment variable is absent. Both issues are scoped to the newly added tests.
